note: Phase A2 asks for a frame-time A/B between the immediate and metered GPU commit paths. It was attempted and could not be completed: the browser this project previews in reports the page as hidden, so requestAnimationFrame does not run and the renderer collects no frame samples. The production default is unchanged.
host: Apple M3 Max, Chromium 152, preview pane
whyBlocked: document.hidden reports true even with the pane fronted, and a 2-second requestAnimationFrame probe recorded 0 frames.
The app's own PERF readout stays at '(collecting...)', so the renderer's frame-time aggregate never received a sample.
draw calls and shown-point counts were identical across a 3-second interval, which is a stalled render loop rather than a steady one.
Without frame samples there is no p50, p95, p99, max, or count of frames over 33 and 50 ms, and those are the metrics that decide this phase.

whatWasObservable.note: Streaming is driven by network and workers rather than by the frame loop, so these remained meaningful. They describe the immediate path on a warm cache and are not an A/B.
whatWasObservable.cache: warm from earlier runs in the same session

decision: The metered commit path stays opt-in. The phase's own rule is that no aesthetic judgement is sufficient and the default moves only on measured evidence, so an unmeasurable environment leaves the default where it is.
whatWouldUnblock: A browser window that is genuinely visible, driven by the user or by a Playwright run with a headed window, so requestAnimationFrame runs and the renderer's frame aggregate fills.
The same deterministic trace under both commit modes on a warm cache, then again cold.
A second device class, since the phase asks for a discrete GPU, an integrated one and a mobile class, and only one machine was available.
